blocks.text: Shivalik Bimetal Controls (SBCL) joins dissimilar metals and sells the result as strip, finished components and, since FY26, small assemblies [F] (AR2026 p.23). It has three established product lines: thermostatic bimetal/trimetal strip and parts made by high-pressure diffusion bonding; electron-beam-welded (EBW) low-ohmic shunt resistors (strip and finished resistors); and silver electrical contacts, made in the wholly owned subsidiary Shivalik Engineered Products (SEPPL) [F] (AR2026 p.23-24). A fourth line, busbar connectors, cell-contacting-system (CCS) assemblies and PCB assemblies, is being built at a new Pune facility [F] (AR2026 p.24, p.39). The company earns its money mainly on conversion value: customers pay for metal, and the company says raw-material costs are passed through [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Nov 2025).

blocks.text: End markets as indicated by management: switchgear absorbs about 80% of bimetal sales, and about 60% of contacts revenue also goes into switchgear, so switchgear-linked demand is 45-50% of total revenue [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Aug 2026). For shunts, about 60% goes to automotive and about 35% to energy meters [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Revenue from smart-meter applications was Rs 75-80 crore in FY26, up from Rs 30-40 crore [MC] (CALL May 2026; AR2026 p.13). The audited accounts report a single operating segment, so none of these end-market splits is audited [F] (AR2026 p.216, p.40).

Source for the geography table is the audited consolidated note [F] (AR2026 p.217). On this basis exports were about 47% of consolidated FY26 revenue [E] (AR2026 p.217). The widely quoted '57% exports' is a standalone figure (56.65%) [F] (AR2026 p.92), even though the annual report also presents it alongside consolidated figures [F] (AR2026 p.38). The company says it has 300+ OEM and Tier-1 customers in 38 countries [MC] (AR2026 p.8). One customer contributed Rs 100.2 crore, or 17.54% of consolidated revenue, in FY26, against 13.47% in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.217).

Listing status: this is not a recent listing. The stock has traded for decades (BSE code 513097; the presentation timeline puts the NSE listing at 2002) [F] (AR2026 p.76; PPT Aug 2026). The evidence base covers ten years of statements [F] (NUMBERS). What is recent is the ownership and leadership change: promoter holding fell from 51.14% to 33.18% in the September 2024 quarter [F] (NUMBERS), and both sons of the chairman joined the board in September and November 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.84).

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: (1) mix shift: company-specific; (2) spare capacity: company-specific; (3) US customer recovery: partly cyclical (inventory, tariffs) and partly company-specific (new patented designs at the customer); (4) smart meters: structural (localisation policy), cyclical in timing; (5) Pune assemblies: company-specific, riding the structural EV localisation theme; (6) contacts: company-specific volume plus a cyclical silver-price component; (7) balance sheet: company-specific.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation leaves no room for error. At Rs 1,042 the stock trades at 56.6x trailing EPS and 42.8x EV/EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS). Our reverse DCF implies about 87.5% annual sales growth for five years, against 8.9% in the base case [E] (NUMBERS). Even the bull DCF value of Rs 165.6 a share is 84% below the price [E] (NUMBERS).

2. Headline growth is flattered by metal prices and a subsidiary. Of Q1 FY27's Rs 45.6 crore YoY revenue increase, about Rs 30 crore came from contacts, whose revenue roughly 2.5x'd [E] (PPT Aug 2026). Management attributes about half of that revenue growth to silver prices [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Standalone revenue grew 12.95% [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

3. Volumes are flat to down. FY26 standalone volumes fell 0.6% [F] (AR2026 p.49). Shunt kg fell 2.2% in FY26 and 11.06% in Q1 FY27 [F] (AR2026 p.43; PPT Aug 2026). India bimetal revenue fell 7.7% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.40). The volume series also changed basis to include wastage [MC] (CALL May 2026).

4. Cash conversion weakened sharply. FY26 CFO was Rs 55 crore against PAT of Rs 96 crore (0.57x) [F] (NUMBERS). Receivables rose Rs 44 crore and inventories Rs 22 crore [F] (AR2026 p.183). Net working capital reached 258 days (standalone basis) after the CFO said in February it would return to the prior year's range by March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.26) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

5. Customer concentration is rising, not falling. The largest customer was 17.54% of consolidated and 21.68% of standalone revenue in FY26, up from 13.47% and 15.67% [F] (AR2026 p.217, p.169). Management expects the US shunt customer to roughly double its business [MC] (CALL May 2026).

6. Governance and finance-function churn. The statutory auditor resigned on 6 August 2026 citing resources [F] (AR2026 p.239). Management thanked the CFO for 'his contribution' and promised an 'orderly finance transition' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The company secretary resigned effective 7 December 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). All three executive directors are one family, and the governance report says there are no inter-se relationships among directors while the remuneration annexure says the chairman is father of the MD and WTD [F] (AR2026 p.74, p.90).

7. Guidance on the new business keeps moving. Year-one assembly revenue was Rs 50-70 crore (PCBA, Nov 2025), then Rs 70-80 crore (Feb 2026), then 10-15% of Rs 300-400 crore (Aug 2026), while the three-year figure rose from Rs 250-300 crore to Rs 300-400 crore [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Feb 2026; CALL Aug 2026). The main Pune facility will be fully operational only in October 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

8. Mix is margin-dilutive at the consolidated level. Consolidated gross margin fell 119 bps YoY to 43.40% in Q1 FY27 [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Busbar assemblies are guided at about 12-13% EBITDA [MC] (AR2026 p.43). Contacts are described as low-margin [MC] (CALL May 2026).

9. Dilution optionality without a stated need. Shareholders amended the Articles on 2 September 2026 to enable warrants and convertibles 'for future capital raising' [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS; AR2026 p.240), although the company calls itself net cash and self-funding [MC] (AR2026 p.38).

10. Single-region manufacturing and tariff exposure. Core plants are in Solan, Himachal Pradesh [F] (AR2026 p.79). US strip shipments fall under 50% Section 232 tariffs on copper and steel [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Is 20-30% FY27 growth organic? Bull: Q1 grew 33.4% and management guides 20-30% [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Bear: standalone grew 13%, and the rest is mainly silver-inflated contacts revenue [E] (PPT Aug 2026). The market may be capitalising commodity-inflated revenue [AI].

Is the margin step-up structural? Bull: standalone gross margin is up about 490 bps in two years (46.57% FY25 to 51.48% Q1 FY27) [E] (AR2026 p.25; PPT Aug 2026). Bear: consolidated gross margin is down YoY in Q1, and FY26 consolidated EBITDA benefited from Rs 4.2 crore lower sales commission [F] (AR2026 p.212). We think the standalone improvement looks durable but consolidated margins will drift down as contacts and assemblies grow [AI].

Concentration: management says the largest customer will stay below 17-18% [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), but it was already 17.54% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.217). Either the largest customer is not the US shunt account, or the ceiling is already reached. The documents do not resolve this [AI].

Pune: is it a real business or a narrative? Real: consent to operate, one programme in production, Rs 20-25 crore capex [F] (PPT Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Unproven: no disclosed order value, customer or revenue, and year-one targets keep shifting [AI].

Valuation: the market may be pricing the company as an electrification platform. Our model prices it as a 9% grower at 21% margins and a 15% WACC [F] (NUMBERS). The gap is too large to close on near-term earnings [AI].

blocks.text: Our variant view [AI]: SBCL is a good niche business in two mature strip technologies (bimetal and EBW shunts) and is improving its mix. The stock, however, is priced as if the Pune assembly business and the US customer recovery were already contracted, multi-hundred-crore revenue streams. They are disclosed only as management ranges with no order book [F] (AR2026 p.46). The overlooked facts point the other way: FY26 cash conversion was weak, concentration on the largest customer is rising, the auditor and CFO are changing, and silver price inflation flatters FY27 growth. On the other side, the bear case may underrate how much standalone EBITDA margin (27.5% in Q1 FY27) [F] (PPT Aug 2026) can compound if components keep displacing strip.

subsections.title: How recent is the current business?

blocks.text: The legacy bimetal business is four decades old, but most of what drives the investment case is recent [AI]. Shunts date from 2015 [F] (AR2026 p.39). Contacts have been consolidated only since FY23, and that partly explains the jump in sales from Rs 324 crore to Rs 470 crore that year [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.57) [AI]. The component-led shunt mix is a 2024-26 development [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Assemblies started in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.41), and the current executive team took board seats in late 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.84). Five-year growth rates (sales 22.9%) therefore mix acquisition, a customer boom-bust and organic growth; the three-year sales CAGR is 6.7% [F] (NUMBERS).

items: 1. Procure alloys: nickel alloys, copper and copper alloys (including manganin for shunts), stainless steel and silver; a large share is imported [MC] (AR2026 p.44; CALL Aug 2026; CALL Nov 2025).
2. Bond or weld: high-pressure diffusion bonding or cold bonding for bimetal/trimetal strip; strip EBW for shunt material [F] (AR2026 p.23, p.37).
3. Precision strip processing: slitting, levelling, tension control [MC] (PPT Aug 2026).
4. Stamping, tooling and finishing into parts, with in-house stamping, tool-room and reliability testing [MC] (AR2026 p.43).
5. For contacts (SEPPL), braze, weld or clad silver alloys onto copper substrates and join them onto stampings [F] (AR2026 p.24).
6. Assemble busbars, CCS and PCBA at Pune, buying PCBs and wiring from outside and integrating in-house shunts and connectors [F] (RATING).
7. Ship to OEM and Tier-1 customers; development cycles of 18-24 months and roughly 24-month re-qualification [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; AR2026 p.37).

blocks.text: Value is captured at the joining step, where weld or bond quality determines current-sensing accuracy and thermal behaviour [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), and at component conversion, where finished parts carry 'nearly double' the value add of strip [MC] (CALL May 2026). The financial evidence is consistent with this. Standalone gross margin (49.39%) is above consolidated (45.21%) because contacts carry precious-metal pass-through [F] (AR2026 p.42) [MC] (CALL May 2026). In assemblies, 60-65% of value is bought-in material [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), so value capture per rupee of revenue is structurally lower [AI].

Outsourced job work was Rs 3.9 crore and contract labour Rs 9.2 crore in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.212). Fixed-asset turnover was 3.81x in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS), and the company says Pune needs only Rs 20-25 crore because the costly EBW capacity already sits in Solan [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Working capital is the real capital intensity: inventory alone was Rs 153 crore against net fixed assets of Rs 122 crore [F] (AR2026 p.183). We class the model as light on fixed assets but heavy on working capital [AI].

blocks.text: Commodity-like [AI]: EBW shunt strip, which management itself says can be sourced from a competitor [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); standard silver contacts, where pricing is metal-plus-surcharge [MC] (CALL May 2026); and generic PCB assembly. Differentiated [AI]: proprietary bimetal grades designed into switchgear at specification stage [MC] (AR2026 p.23), and precision EBW shunt components where accuracy, not price, decides supplier choice [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The mix is shifting towards differentiated shunt components and, at the same time, towards commodity-like contacts and assemblies. The net effect is visible in standalone gross margin rising while consolidated gross margin fell in Q1 FY27 [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

items: Shunts, management view: India demand from smart meters, automotive and BMS; conversion of strip to parts; the US customer recovering in component form [MC] (AR2026 p.12; CALL Aug 2026). About 70-75% of Q1 shunt growth is attributed to value addition and the rest to commodity prices [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Our read: realisation per kg rose about 33% YoY in Q1 while kg fell 11% [E] (PPT Aug 2026). Some of that is copper pass-through, and part of the kg decline reflects the shrinking strip business [AI].

Bimetals, management view: Indian MCB consumption is flat because the real-estate boom is concentrated in luxury housing; US developments were paused by tariffs [MC] (CALL May 2026). In August, management reported the first volume uptick in 4-5 quarters [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Our read: FY26 growth came entirely from Europe (+Rs 16 crore) while India fell Rs 9 crore [F] (AR2026 p.25). Management claims about 90% domestic share [MC] (CALL May 2026), so growth depends on market growth plus exports [AI].

Contacts, management view: about 31-32 points of the roughly 60% growth was business growth and the rest silver [MC] (CALL May 2026), helped by new plant capacity [MC] (CALL May 2026). Our read: the disclosed SEPPL figure is +54.9% [F] (AR2026 p.50). Management quoted both 60% and 54% [MC] (CALL May 2026), which is not reconciled, and silver has 'more than doubled' YoY [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

blocks.text: None of the segments runs on a disclosed order book [F] (AR2026 p.46). Shunts and bimetals sell against customer schedules and forecasts on long-running part numbers [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), so they behave like organic run-rate businesses with customer-specific step changes (for example the Vishay destock) [AI]. Assemblies are programme-driven: revenue depends on the volumes of specific EV models [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

We use only the base case of our DCF model [F] (NUMBERS): a five-year free cash flow to the firm (FCFF) projection from TTM sales of Rs 616 crore. summary.one_line: Shivalik Bimetal is a real process-niche business with a genuine shift to higher-value components and a net-cash balance sheet, but at Rs 1,042 it is priced for about 88% annual growth while silver-inflated revenue, weak FY26 cash conversion, rising customer concentration and simultaneous auditor/CFO/CS changes argue that the evidence lags the price by a wide margin.
bull_points: Mix shift to components is lifting value per kg: standalone gross margin rose from 46.57% (FY25) to 49.39% (FY26) and 51.48% in Q1 FY27 [F] (AR2026 p.25; PPT Aug 2026); standalone gross contribution per kg rose about 13% on flat material cost per kg [E] (AR2026 p.25, p.138).

Spare capacity with low capex needs: management says the asset base supports over Rs 1,300 crore of revenue, with bimetal utilisation at 40-45% and maintenance capex of Rs 10-15 crore a year [MC] (AR2026 p.43; CALL Aug 2026; CALL May 2026).
Q1 FY27 showed the US recovery starting: Americas shunt revenue +30%, consolidated revenue +33.4%, EBITDA +35% and PAT +45% [F] (PPT Aug 2026).
Net-cash balance sheet: cash and bank of Rs 104.7 crore vs bank debt of Rs 59.4 crore; ROCE 27%; Crisil A/Stable [F] (AR2026 p.183, p.206; NUMBERS; RATING).
Growth options in smart-meter localisation (smart-meter revenue Rs 75-80 crore and expected to double) and Pune EV assemblies (Rs 300-400 crore potential) [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026).
bear_points: Valuation: the reverse DCF implies about 87.5% annual sales growth for five years vs 8.9% in the base case; bear/base/bull fair values of Rs 77.6/125.7/165.6 are 84-93% below the price [F] (NUMBERS).

Growth quality: about two-thirds of Q1 FY27's revenue increase came from the contacts subsidiary [E] (PPT Aug 2026), about half of whose growth management attributes to silver prices [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). FY26 standalone volumes fell 0.6% and Q1 shunt kg fell 11% [F] (AR2026 p.49; PPT Aug 2026).

Cash conversion: FY26 CFO of Rs 55 crore vs PAT of Rs 96 crore (0.57x); NWC rose from 218 to 258 days despite February guidance to return to the prior-year range [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.26) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Concentration rising: the largest customer rose from 13.47% to 17.54% of consolidated revenue (21.68% standalone), contradicting management's 'about 13-14%' in May 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.217, p.169) [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Governance churn: the statutory auditor resigned on 6 Aug 2026, a CFO transition was flagged, and the CS resigned effective 7 Dec 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.239; ANNOUNCEMENTS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The Articles now enable warrants and convertibles [F] (AR2026 p.240).
